Getting started with bourse

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd
library(bourse)

What bourse does

bourse is the market-data connector of the ORCHESTRA analytics framework: it fetches cryptocurrency OHLCV candles from public exchange APIs and returns them as a contract-typed, provenance-labelled series. It is the trading-domain counterpart of the terroir geo-data collector, and it is built around one discipline – the Independent Oracle Principle (IOP): a fact about an exchange (a symbol, a price tick size, a fee, a column’s unit) is unverified until it has been diffed against the exchange’s own catalogue. For a trading system that is risk control, not bookkeeping: an unverified tick size or fee is a silently wrong number that loses money.

Two outcomes: a series, or a refusal

bourse_ohlcv() returns either a grounded market_series or a bourse_refusal. It refuses rather than returning a number it cannot stand behind. Here we parse a recorded candle fixture offline (the live path uses the suggested httr2).

fixture <- cbind(
  open_time = c(1.5e12, 1.5e12 + 86400000),
  open = c(100, 102), high = c(105, 106), low = c(99, 101),
  close = c(102, 104), volume = c(1200, 1500))

series <- bourse_ohlcv("BTCUSDT", interval = "1d", candles = fixture)
series
#> <market_series> BTCUSDT @ binance [1d]  2 rows  [[unverified]]
series@grounding
#> [1] "[unverified]"

The series is [unverified] – not because the candles are wrong, but because nothing has yet confirmed that this symbol, its tick size, and the column meaning match the exchange’s catalogue. A consumer on a live order path gates on this.

An unknown source, or malformed candles, is refused:

bourse_ohlcv("BTCUSDT", candles = fixture, source = "nasdaq")
#> <bourse_refusal: unknown_source> no adapter for source 'nasdaq' (nasdaq)

Order books and tickers

The same two-outcome, grounding-carrying contract covers the other read-only endpoints. bourse_orderbook() parses an order book (/api/v3/depth) and refuses a crossed book; bourse_ticker() parses the 24-hour statistics (/api/v3/ticker/24hr). Each carries an obs_schema and a grounding label.

book <- bourse_orderbook("BTCUSDT", depth = list(
  bids = list(c("100.0", "1.5"), c("99.9", "2.0")),
  asks = list(c("100.1", "1.0"), c("100.2", "3.0"))))
book
#> <order_book> BTCUSDT @ binance  2 bids / 2 asks  [[unverified]]

ticker <- bourse_ticker("BTCUSDT", ticker = list(
  symbol = "BTCUSDT", lastPrice = "100.0", openPrice = "98.0",
  highPrice = "101.0", lowPrice = "97.0", volume = "1200",
  quoteVolume = "118800", openTime = 1.5e12, closeTime = 1.5e12 + 86400000))
ticker
#> <market_ticker> BTCUSDT @ binance  last=100  24h=NA%  [[unverified]]

A crossed book – best bid at or above best ask – is a structural impossibility for a resting book, so it is refused rather than returned:

bourse_orderbook("BTCUSDT", depth = list(
  bids = list(c("101.0", "1.0")), asks = list(c("100.0", "1.0"))))
#> <bourse_refusal: crossed_book> best bid is not below best ask; refusing a crossed book (binance)

The provenance registry

Every fact bourse asserts is in a registry, with the date it was last checked. Until the oracle runs, every family is [unverified]:

bourse_fact_status("binance")
#>    source n_facts n_grounded n_unverified
#> 1 binance      10          0           10

The fee_schedule family is deliberately never grounded here: its authority is the authenticated /sapi/v1/asset/tradeFee endpoint, which would introduce an API-credential surface. bourse reads public, anonymous endpoints only, so the fee schedule stays [unverified] rather than substituting a documentation default it cannot diff against the account’s actual fee tier.

Grounding: the catalogue-diff oracle

bourse_catalogue_diff() is the only operation that grounds a fact. It diffs the asserted facts against the exchange’s own /exchangeInfo catalogue (here a recorded catalogue shape; live by default). Families that agree are grounded with a real date; the rest stay [unverified].

info <- list(symbols = list(list(
  symbol = "BTCUSDT", baseAsset = "BTC", quoteAsset = "USDT",
  filters = list(
    list(filterType = "PRICE_FILTER", tickSize = "0.01"),
    list(filterType = "LOT_SIZE", stepSize = "0.00001"),
    list(filterType = "NOTIONAL", minNotional = "5")))))

bourse_catalogue_diff("binance", symbols = "BTCUSDT", exchange_info = info)
#>                  fact_family   status
#> 1            symbol_universe grounded
#> 2                  tick_size grounded
#> 3                   lot_size grounded
#> 4               min_notional grounded
#> 5        quote_base_currency grounded
#> 6     ohlcv_column_semantics grounded
#> 7 orderbook_column_semantics grounded
#> 8    ticker_column_semantics grounded
#> 9               timestamp_tz grounded
#>                                                detail
#> 1 agreed against recorded exchange_info on 2026-10-29
#> 2 agreed against recorded exchange_info on 2026-10-29
#> 3 agreed against recorded exchange_info on 2026-10-29
#> 4 agreed against recorded exchange_info on 2026-10-29
#> 5 agreed against recorded exchange_info on 2026-10-29
#> 6 agreed against recorded exchange_info on 2026-10-29
#> 7 agreed against recorded exchange_info on 2026-10-29
#> 8 agreed against recorded exchange_info on 2026-10-29
#> 9 agreed against recorded exchange_info on 2026-10-29

Now the same series is grounded, because the facts it rests on have been verified against the authority:

bourse_ohlcv("BTCUSDT", candles = fixture)@grounding
#> [1] "grounded"

Why this matters for the orchestra

bourse feeds the trading members (kalmix, proxymix) and the decideR decision layer. Because the series carries its grounding label, an un-grounded price feed propagates worst-case through the pipeline and decideR forces a flat position – the capital firewall. Reporting what is not grounded is the trading system’s risk control.
